core.title: Chemical Compositions Of Red Giant Stars in the Old Open Cluster NGC 7789
core.venue: Astronomical Journal
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The Wall Street Neophyte: A Zero-Shot Analysis of ChatGPT Over MultiModal Stock Movement Prediction Challenges

core.title: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work presents BloombergGPT, a 50 billion parameter language model that is trained on a wide range of financial data, and constructs a 363 billion token dataset based on Bloomberg's extensive data sources, perhaps the largest domain-specific dataset yet.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: BloombergGPT: A Large Language Model for Finance

core.title: Numerical Correlation in Text
core.venue: MATHNLP
core.summary: A new task, Numerical Correlation in Text, which requires models to identify the correlation between two numbers in a sentence is proposed and a new dataset is introduced, which contains over 2,000 Wikipedia sentences with two numbers and their correlation labels.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Numerical Correlation in Text

core.title: Assessing the Importance of Frequency versus Compositionality for Subword-based Tokenization in NMT
core.venue: European Association for Machine Translation Conferences/Workshops
core.summary: A tokenization approach is proposed that enables us to separate frequency (the first advantage) from compositionality, thanks to the use of Huffman coding, which tokenizes words using a fixed amount of symbols.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Assessing the Importance of Frequency versus Compositionality for Subword-based Tokenization in NMT

core.title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: A strong logistic regression model is built, which achieves an F1 score of 51.0%, a significant improvement over a simple baseline (20%).
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text

core.title: SberQuAD - Russian Reading Comprehension Dataset: Description and Analysis
core.venue: Conference and Labs of the Evaluation Forum
core.summary: SberQuAD -- a large scale analog of Stanford SQuAD in the Russian language - is a valuable resource that has not been properly presented to the scientific community by providing a description, a thorough analysis, and baseline experimental results.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: SberQuAD -- Russian Reading Comprehension Dataset: Description and Analysis

core.title: MANTa: Efficient Gradient-Based Tokenization for End-to-End Robust Language Modeling
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: MANTa: Efficient Gradient-Based Tokenization for End-to-End Robust Language Modeling

core.title: RetVec: Resilient and Efficient Text Vectorizer
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: Evaluated and compared RETVec to state-of-the-art vectorizers and word embeddings on popular model architectures and datasets demonstrate thatRETVec leads to competitive, multilingual models that are significantly more resilient to typos and adversarial text attacks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: RetVec: Resilient and Efficient Text Vectorizer

core.title: CharacterBERT: Reconciling ELMo and BERT for Word-Level Open-Vocabulary Representations From Characters
core.venue: International Conference on Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work proposes CharacterBERT, a new variant of BERT that drops the wordpiece system altogether and uses a Character-CNN module instead to represent entire words by consulting their characters, and shows that this new model improves the performance of Bert on a variety of medical domain tasks while at the same time producing robust, word-level, and open-vocabulary representations.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: CharacterBERT: Reconciling ELMo and BERT for Word-Level Open-Vocabulary Representations From Characters

core.title: Do NLP Models Know Numbers? Probing Numeracy in Embeddings
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work investigates the numerical reasoning capabilities of a state-of-the-art question answering model on the DROP dataset and finds this model excels on questions that require numerical reasoning, i.e., it already captures numeracy.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Do NLP Models Know Numbers? Probing Numeracy in Embeddings

core.title: GPT-4 Technical Report
core.summary: GPT-4, a large-scale, multimodal model which can accept image and text inputs and produce text outputs, is developed, a Transformer-based model pre-trained to predict the next token in a document which exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: GPT-4 Technical Report

core.title: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A simple regularization method is presented, subword regularization, which trains the model with multiple subword segmentations probabilistically sampled during training, and a new sub word segmentation algorithm based on a unigram language model is proposed.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Subword Regularization: Improving Neural Network Translation Models with Multiple Subword Candidates

core.title: Google's Neural Machine Translation System: Bridging the Gap between Human and Machine Translation
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: GNMT, Google's Neural Machine Translation system, is presented, which attempts to address many of the weaknesses of conventional phrase-based translation systems and provides a good balance between the flexibility of "character"-delimited models and the efficiency of "word"-delicited models.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Google's neural machine translation system: Bridging the gap between human and machine translation

core.title: MEGABYTE: Predicting Million-byte Sequences with Multiscale Transformers
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: Megabyte, a multi-scale decoder architecture that enables end-to-end differentiable modeling of sequences of over one million bytes, is proposed, establishing the viability of tokenization-free autoregressive sequence modeling at scale.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Megabyte: Predicting million-byte sequences with multiscale transformers

core.title: Between words and characters: A Brief History of Open-Vocabulary Modeling and Tokenization in NLP
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: It is concluded that there is and likely will never be a silver bullet singular solution for all applications and that thinking seriously about tokenization remains important for many applications.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Between words and characters: A brief history of open-vocabulary modeling and tokenization in NLP

core.title: Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work synthesizes best practices for representing numbers in text and articulate a vision for holistic numeracy in NLP, comprised of design trade-offs and a unified evaluation.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Representing Numbers in NLP: a Survey and a Vision

core.title: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper shows that a standard Transformer architecture can be used with minimal modifications to process byte sequences, characterize the trade-offs in terms of parameter count, training FLOPs, and inference speed, and shows that byte-level models are competitive with their token-level counterparts.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: ByT5: Towards a Token-Free Future with Pre-trained Byte-to-Byte Models

core.title: Canine: Pre-training an Efficient Tokenization-Free Encoder for Language Representation
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Canine is presented, a neural encoder that operates directly on character sequences—without explicit tokenization or vocabulary—and a pre-training strategy that operates either directly on characters or optionally uses subwords as a soft inductive bias.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Canine: Pre-training an Efficient Tokenization-Free Encoder for Language Representation

core.title: Sub-Character Tokenization for Chinese Pretrained Language Models
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Experimental results show that SubChar tokenizers have two main advantages over existing tokenizers: 1) They can tokenize inputs into much shorter sequences, thus improving the computational efficiency, and 2) Pronunciation-based SubChartokenization can encode Chinese homophones into the same transliteration sequences and produce the same tokenization output, hence being robust to homophone typos.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: SHUOWEN-JIEZI: Linguistically informed tokenizers for Chinese language model pretraining

core.title: BPE beyond Word Boundary: How NOT to use Multi Word Expressions in Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: First Workshop on Insights from Negative Results in NLP
core.summary: This work observes that naively extending BPE beyond word boundaries results in incoherent tokens which are themselves better represented as individual words, and finds that Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) instead of frequency finds better MWEs (e.g., New\_York, Statue of Liberty, neither .
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: BPE beyond Word Boundary: How NOT to use Multi Word Expressions in Neural Machine Translation

core.title: Robust Open-Vocabulary Translation from Visual Text Representations
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work proposes the use of visual text representations, which dispense with a finite set of text embeddings in favor of continuous vocabularies created by processing visually rendered text with sliding windows, and demonstrates significant robustness to varied types of noise.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Robust Open-Vocabulary Translation from Visual Text Representations

core.title: Language Modelling with Pixels
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: PIXEL is a pretrained language model that renders text as images, making it possible to transfer representations across languages based on orthographic similarity or the co-activation of pixels, and is more robust than BERT to orthographic attacks and linguistic code-switching, further confirming the benefits of modelling language with pixels.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Language Modelling with Pixels

core.title: What do tokens know about their characters and how do they know it?
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: The mechanisms through which PLMs acquire English-language character information during training are investigated and it is argued that this knowledge is acquired through multiple phenomena, including a systematic relationship between particular characters and particular parts of speech, as well as natural variability in the tokenization of related strings.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: What do tokens know about their characters and how do they know it?

core.title: BPE-Dropout: Simple and Effective Subword Regularization
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: BPE-dropout is introduced - simple and effective subword regularization method based on and compatible with conventional BPE that stochastically corrupts the segmentation procedure of BPE, which leads to producing multiple segmentations within the same fixed BPE framework.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: BPE-Dropout: Simple and Effective Subword Regularization

core.title: Multi-view Subword Regularization
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: To take full advantage of different possible input segmentations, the proposed Multi-view Subword Regularization (MVR) method enforces the consistency of predictors between using inputs tokenized by the standard and probabilistic segmentations.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Multi-view Subword Regularization

core.title: Numeracy enhances the Literacy of Language Models
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: A significant improvement in MWP for sentences containing numbers is found, that exponent embeddings are the best number encoders, yielding over 2 points jump in prediction accuracy over a BERT baseline, and that these enhanced literacy skills also generalize to contexts without annotated numbers.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Numeracy enhances the Literacy of Language Models

core.title: Patient Inertia and the Status Quo Bias
core.venue: Psychology Science
core.summary: A laboratory analogue of the decision context that frequently occurs in situations involving patient inertia was created, and it was examined whether participants would stay with a default option even when it was clearly inferior to other available options.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Patient Inertia and the Status Quo Bias

core.title: Do All Languages Cost the Same? Tokenization in the Era of Commercial Language Models
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work conducts a systematic analysis of the cost and utility of OpenAI's language model API on multilingual benchmarks in 22 typologically diverse languages and shows evidence that speakers of a large number of the supported languages are overcharged while obtaining poorer results.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Do All Languages Cost the Same? Tokenization in the Era of Commercial Language Models

core.title: No Language Left Behind: Scaling Human-Centered Machine Translation
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: A conditional compute model based on Sparsely Gated Mixture of Experts that is trained on data obtained with novel and effective data mining techniques tailored for low-resource languages is developed, laying important groundwork towards realizing a universal translation system.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: No Language Left Behind: Scaling Human-Centered Machine Translation

core.title: Estimating Numbers without Regression
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: A carefully designed tokenization scheme is both the simplest to implement and sufficient, with similar performance to the state-of-the-art approach that requires making significant architectural changes, in the context of masked number prediction.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Estimating Numbers without Regression

core.title: Getting the most out of your tokenizer for pre-training and domain adaptation
core.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning
core.summary: It is shown that the size, pre-tokenization regular expression, and training data of a tokenizer can significantly impact the model's generation speed, effective context size, memory usage, and downstream performance.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Getting the most out of your tokenizer for pre-training and domain adaptation

core.title: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)
core.summary: An empirical evaluation of the GELU nonlinearity against the ReLU and ELU activations is performed and performance improvements are found across all considered computer vision, natural language processing, and speech tasks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Gaussian Error Linear Units (GELUs)

core.title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: LLaMA, a collection of foundation language models ranging from 7B to 65B parameters, is introduced and it is shown that it is possible to train state-of-the-art models using publicly available datasets exclusively, without resorting to proprietary and inaccessible datasets.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models

core.title: Mistral 7B
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work introduces Mistral 7B v0.1, a 7-billion-parameter language model engineered for superior performance and efficiency, which leverages grouped-query attention (GQA) for faster inference, coupled with sliding window attention (SWA) to effectively handle sequences of arbitrary length with a reduced inference cost.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Mistral 7B

core.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: GPT-3 achieves strong performance on many NLP datasets, including translation, question-answering, and cloze tasks, as well as several tasks that require on-the-fly reasoning or domain adaptation, such as unscrambling words, using a novel word in a sentence, or performing 3-digit arithmetic.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners

core.title: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: OLMo is built, a competitive, truly Open Language Model, to enable the scientific study of language models and it is hoped this release will empower the open research community and inspire a new wave of innovation.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: OLMo: Accelerating the Science of Language Models

core.title: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work develops and releases Llama 2, a collection of pretrained and fine-tuned large language models (LLMs) ranging in scale from 7 billion to 70 billion parameters, which may be a suitable substitute for closed-source models.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Llama 2: Open Foundation and Fine-Tuned Chat Models

core.title: Two New Evaluation Datasets for Low-Resource Machine Translation: Nepali-English and Sinhala-English
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work takes sentences from Wikipedia pages and introduces new evaluation datasets in two very low resource language pairs, Nepali-English and Sinhala-English, and describes the process to collect and cross-check the quality of translations and reports baseline performance using several learning settings.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: No Language Left Behind: Scaling Human-Centered Machine Translation

core.title: compare-mt: A Tool for Holistic Comparison of Language Generation Systems
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: compare-mt: A Tool for Holistic Comparison of Language Generation Systems

core.title: chrF: character n-gram F-score for automatic MT evaluation
core.venue: WMT@EMNLP
core.summary: The proposed use of character n-gram F-score for automatic evaluation of machine translation output shows very promising results, especially for the CHRF3 score – for translation from English, this variant showed the highest segment-level correlations outperforming even the best metrics on the WMT14 shared evaluation task.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: chrF: character n-gram F-score for automatic MT evaluation

core.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper introduces a simpler and more effective approach, making the NMT model capable of open-vocabulary translation by encoding rare and unknown words as sequences of subword units, and empirically shows that subword models improve over a back-off dictionary baseline for the WMT 15 translation tasks English-German and English-Russian by 1.3 BLEU.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units

core.title: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores
core.venue: Conference on Machine Translation
core.summary: Pointing to the success of the parsing community, it is suggested machine translation researchers settle upon the BLEU scheme, which does not allow for user-supplied reference processing, and provide a new tool, SACREBLEU, to facilitate this.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: A Call for Clarity in Reporting BLEU Scores

core.title: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: This work introduces Adam, an algorithm for first-order gradient-based optimization of stochastic objective functions, based on adaptive estimates of lower-order moments, and provides a regret bound on the convergence rate that is comparable to the best known results under the online convex optimization framework.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization

core.title: Findings of the 2022 Conference on Machine Translation (WMT22)
core.venue: Conference on Machine Translation
core.summary: This paper evaluates system outputs with human annotators using two different techniques: reference-based direct assessment and (DA) and a combination of DA and scalar quality metric (DA+SQM).
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Findings of the 2022 Conference on Machine Translation (WMT22)

core.title: Many-to-English Machine Translation Tools, Data, and Pretrained Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work creates a multilingual neural machine translation model capable of translating from 500 source languages to English, readily downloadable and usable as a service, or as a parent model for transfer-learning to even lower-resource languages.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Many-to-English Machine Translation Tools, Data, and Pretrained Models

core.title: Toucan: Token-Aware Character Level Language Modeling
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: Toucan is proposed, an augmentation to character-level models to make them "token-aware", demonstrating significant speed-ups in character generation without a loss in language modeling performance.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Toucan: Token-Aware Character Level Language Modeling

core.title: Are Character-level Translations Worth the Wait? Comparing ByT5 and mT5 for Machine Translation
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work performs an extensive comparison across multiple languages and experimental conditions of character- and subword-level pretrained models (ByT5 and mT5, respectively) on NMT, and shows the effectiveness of character-level modeling in translation, particularly in cases where fine-tuning data is limited.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Are Character-level Translations Worth the Wait? Comparing Character- and Subword-level Models for Machine Translation

core.title: Alternation
core.venue: JACM
core.summary: It is shown that alternating pushdown automata are strictly more powerful than nondeterministic pushdown Automata and the number of alternations allowed during computations.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Alternation

core.title: Yara Parser: A Fast and Accurate Dependency Parser
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: The Yara Parser is introduced, a fast and accurate open-source dependency parser based on the arc-eager algorithm and beam search that achieves an unlabeled accuracy of 93.32 on the standard WSJ test set which ranks it among the top dependency parsers.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Yara Parser: A Fast and Accurate Dependency Parser

core.title: Are Discrete Units Necessary for Spoken Language Modeling?
core.venue: IEEE Journal on Selected Topics in Signal Processing
core.summary: This work shows that discretization is indeed essential for good results in spoken language modeling, and removes linguistically irrelevant information from the continuous features, helping to improve language modeling performances.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Are discrete units necessary for Spoken Language Modeling?

core.title: Learning to Look Inside: Augmenting Token-Based Encoders with Character-Level Information
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: It is shown that incorporating XRayEmb's learned vectors into sequences of pre- trained token embeddings helps performance on both autoregressive and masked pre-trained transformer architectures and on both sequence-level and sequence tagging tasks, particularly on non-standard English text.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Learning to Look Inside: Augmenting Token-Based Encoders with Character-Level Information

core.title: The Wall Street Neophyte: A Zero-Shot Analysis of ChatGPT Over MultiModal Stock Movement Prediction Challenges
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: It is indicated that ChatGPT is a "Wall Street Neophyte" with limited success in predicting stock movements, as it underperforms not only state-of-the-art methods but also traditional methods like linear regression using price features.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The wall street neophyte: A zero-shot analysis of chatgpt over multimodal stock movement prediction challenges

core.title: Enhancing Quantitative Reasoning Skills of Large Language Models through Dimension Perception
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Engineering
core.summary: This work presents a framework to enhance the quantitative reasoning ability of language models based on dimension perception and proposes a benchmark DimEval consisting of seven tasks of three categories to probe and enhance the dimension perception skills of LLMs.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Enhancing Quantitative Reasoning Skills of Large Language Models through Dimension Perception

core.title: Masked Measurement Prediction: Learning to Jointly Predict Quantities and Units from Textual Context
core.venue: NAACL-HLT
core.summary: A new Generative Masked Measurement (GeMM) model is introduced that jointly learns to predict numbers along with their units and linear probing of traditional pretrained transformer models (RoBERTa) is used to show that they significantly underperform jointly trained number-unit models.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Masked Measurement Prediction: Learning to Jointly Predict Quantities and Units from Textual Context

core.title: Numeracy for Language Models: Evaluating and Improving their Ability to Predict Numbers
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper explores different strategies for modelling numerals with language models, such as memorisation and digit-by-digit composition, and proposes a novel neural architecture that uses a continuous probability density function to model numerals from an open vocabulary.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Numeracy for Language Models: Evaluating and Improving their Ability to Predict Numbers

core.title: How Much is 131 Million Dollars? Putting Numbers in Perspective with Compositional Descriptions
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work collects a dataset of numeric mentions in news articles, where each mention is labeled with a set of rated perspectives, and proposes a system to generate short descriptions known as perspectives consisting of two steps: formula construction and description generation.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: How Much is 131 Million Dollars? Putting Numbers in Perspective with Compositional Descriptions

core.title: To Put That in Perspective: Generating Analogies that Make Numbers Easier to Understand
core.venue: International Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
core.summary: This paper systematically test what factors influence the quality of perspective sentences through randomized experiments involving over 1,000 participants and develops a statistical model for generating perspectives and test it against several alternatives, finding beneficial effects of perspectives on comprehension that persist for six weeks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: To Put That in Perspective: Generating Analogies That Make Numbers Easier to Understand

core.title: How Large Are Lions? Inducing Distributions over Quantitative Attributes
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work proposes an unsupervised method for collecting quantitative information from large amounts of web data, and uses it to create a new, very large resource consisting of distributions over physical quantities associated with objects, adjectives, and verbs which it calls Distributions over Quantitative (DoQ).
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: How Large Are Lions? Inducing Distributions over Quantitative Attributes

core.title: How Pre-trained Word Representations Capture Commonsense Physical Comparisons
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work investigates how comparisons are made: models learn a consistent ordering over all the objects in the comparisons and finds probing models have significantly higher accuracy than those baseline models which use dataset artifacts.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: How Pre-trained Word Representations Capture Commonsense Physical Comparisons

core.title: Numeracy-600K: Learning Numeracy for Detecting Exaggerated Information in Market Comments
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper attempts to answer the question of whether neural network models can learn numeracy, which is the ability to predict the magnitude of a numeral at some specific position in a text description, through comprehensive experiments.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Numeracy-600K: Learning Numeracy for Detecting Exaggerated Information in Market Comments

core.title: Exploring Numeracy in Word Embeddings
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Inspired by cognitive studies on how humans perceive numbers, an analysis framework is developed to test how well word embeddings capture two essential properties of numbers: magnitude and numeration.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Exploring Numeracy in Word Embeddings

core.title: “When Numbers Matter!”: Detecting Sarcasm in Numerical Portions of Text
core.venue: WASSA@NAACL-HLT
core.summary: This paper focuses on detecting sarcasm in tweets arising out of numbers, and implements a rule-based and a statistical machine learning-based (ML) classifier that conveys the crux of the numerical sarcasm problem, namely, incongruity arising in numbers.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: ``When Numbers Matter!'': Detecting Sarcasm in Numerical Portions of Text

core.title: NumNet: Machine Reading Comprehension with Numerical Reasoning
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: A numerical MRC model named as NumNet is proposed, which utilizes a numerically-aware graph neural network to consider the comparing information and performs numerical reasoning over numbers in the question and passage, outperforming all existing machine reading comprehension models by considering the numerical relations among numbers.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: NumNet: Machine Reading Comprehension with Numerical Reasoning

core.title: Towards Question Format Independent Numerical Reasoning: A Set of Prerequisite Tasks
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This work introduces NUMBERGAME, a multifaceted benchmark to evaluate model performance across numerical reasoning tasks of eight diverse formats, and takes forward the recent progress in generic system development, demonstrating the scope of under-explored tasks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Towards Question Format Independent Numerical Reasoning: A Set of Prerequisite Tasks

core.title: DROP: A Reading Comprehension Benchmark Requiring Discrete Reasoning Over Paragraphs
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A new reading comprehension benchmark, DROP, which requires Discrete Reasoning Over the content of Paragraphs, and presents a new model that combines reading comprehension methods with simple numerical reasoning to achieve 51% F1.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: DROP: A Reading Comprehension Benchmark Requiring Discrete Reasoning Over Paragraphs

core.title: Giving BERT a Calculator: Finding Operations and Arguments with Reading Comprehension
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work enables a BERT-based reading comprehension model to perform lightweight numerical reasoning by augmenting the model with a predefined set of executable ‘programs’ which encompass simple arithmetic as well as extraction.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Giving BERT a Calculator: Finding Operations and Arguments with Reading Comprehension

core.title: Bootstrapping for Numerical Open IE
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: BONIE is designed and released, the first open numerical relation extractor, for extracting Open IE tuples where one of the arguments is a number or a quantity-unit phrase.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Bootstrapping for Numerical Open IE

core.title: Is a 204 cm Man Tall or Small ? Acquisition of Numerical Common Sense from the Web
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: Novel methods for modeling numerical common sense are presented: the ability to infer whether a given number is large, small, or normal for a given context for aGiven context is presented.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Is a 204 cm Man Tall or Small ? Acquisition of Numerical Common Sense from the Web

core.title: TORQUE: A Reading Comprehension Dataset of Temporal Ordering Questions
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: TORQUE is introduced, a new English reading comprehension benchmark built on 3.2k news snippets with 21k human-generated questions querying temporal relationships, and results show that RoBERTa-large achieves an exact-match score of 51% on the test set of TORQUE, about 30% behind human performance.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: TORQUE: A Reading Comprehension Dataset of Temporal Ordering Questions

core.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: It is found that BERT was significantly undertrained, and can match or exceed the performance of every model published after it, and the best model achieves state-of-the-art results on GLUE, RACE and SQuAD.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach

core.title: BERT in Negotiations: Early Prediction of Buyer-Seller Negotiation Outcomes
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This model is able to predict a negotiation's outcome within 10% for more than 70% of the cases, and suggests that rather than just being a way to realize a negotiation, natural language should be incorporated in the negotiation planning as well.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: BERT in Negotiations: Early Prediction of Buyer-Seller Negotiation Outcomes

core.title: MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A large-scale dataset of math word problems and an interpretable neural math problem solver by learning to map problems to their operation programs and a new representation language to model operation programs corresponding to each math problem that aim to improve both the performance and the interpretability of the learned models.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms

core.title: “Was It Good? It Was Provocative.” Learning the Meaning of Scalar Adjectives
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: It is shown how to ground scalar modifier meaning based on data collected from the Web and that meanings can be learned from Web data and that such meanings can drive pragmatic inference.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: ``Was It Good? It Was Provocative.'' Learning the Meaning of Scalar Adjectives

core.title: Grounding Gradable Adjectives through Crowdsourcing
core.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
core.summary: A method is proposed for estimating concrete groundings for a set of gradable adjectives that can take a range of magnitudes such as small or slight using crowdsourcing to gather human language intuitions about the impact of each adjective and a linear mixed effects model to this data.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Grounding Gradable Adjectives through Crowdsourcing

core.title: From 'F' to 'A' on the N.Y. Regents Science Exams: An Overview of the Aristo Project
core.venue: The AI Magazine
core.summary: Success is reported on the Grade 8 New York Regents Science Exam, where for the first time a system scores more than 90 percent on the exam’s nondiagram, multiple choice (NDMC) questions, demonstrating that modern natural language processing methods can result in mastery on this task.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: From'F'to'A'on the NY Regents Science Exams: An Overview of the Aristo Project

core.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A new language representation model, BERT, designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers, which can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

core.title: NumClaim: Investor's Fine-grained Claim Detection
core.venue: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management
core.summary: A novel task for argument mining in the financial domain, and an expert-annotated dataset, NumClaim, is designed, and it is shown that encoding numeral and co-training with the auxiliary task of the numeral understanding can improve the performance of the proposed task under different neural network architectures.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: NumClaim: Investor's Fine-Grained Claim Detection

core.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: A new global logbilinear regression model that combines the advantages of the two major model families in the literature: global matrix factorization and local context window methods and produces a vector space with meaningful substructure.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

core.title: Deep Contextualized Word Representations
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A new type of deep contextualized word representation is introduced that models both complex characteristics of word use and how these uses vary across linguistic contexts, allowing downstream models to mix different types of semi-supervision signals.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Deep Contextualized Word Representations

core.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: Two novel model architectures for computing continuous vector representations of words from very large data sets are proposed and it is shown that these vectors provide state-of-the-art performance on the authors' test set for measuring syntactic and semantic word similarities.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Efficient estimation of word representations in vector space

core.title: Verb Physics: Relative Physical Knowledge of Actions and Objects
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: An approach to infer relative physical knowledge of actions and objects along five dimensions (e.g., size, weight, and strength) from unstructured natural language text is presented.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Verb Physics: Relative Physical Knowledge of Actions and Objects

core.title: Solving General Arithmetic Word Problems
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This is the first algorithmic approach that can handle arithmetic problems with multiple steps and operations, without depending on additional annotations or predefined templates, and it outperforms existing systems, achieving state of the art performance on benchmark datasets of arithmetic word problems.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Solving General Arithmetic Word Problems

core.title: Temporal Common Sense Acquisition with Minimal Supervision
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work proposes a novel sequence modeling approach that exploits explicit and implicit mentions of temporal common sense, extracted from a large corpus, to build TacoLM, a temporal commonsense language model.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Temporal Common Sense Acquisition with Minimal Supervision

core.title: EQUATE: A Benchmark Evaluation Framework for Quantitative Reasoning in Natural Language Inference
core.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
core.summary: Equal (Evaluating Quantitative Understanding Aptitude in Textual Entailment), a new framework for quantitative reasoning in textual entailment, is presented and it is found that on average, state-of-the-art methods do not achieve an absolute improvement over a majority-class baseline, suggesting that they do not implicitly learn to reason with quantities.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: EQUATE: A Benchmark Evaluation Framework for Quantitative Reasoning in Natural Language Inference

core.title: Reasoning about Quantities in Natural Language
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A computational approach is developed which is shown to successfully recognize and normalize textual expressions of quantities and is used to further develop algorithms to assist reasoning in the context of the aforementioned tasks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Reasoning about Quantities in Natural Language

core.title: SemEval-2018 Task 5: Counting Events and Participants in the Long Tail
core.venue: International Workshop on Semantic Evaluation
core.summary: The design of this referential quantification task of counting events and participants in local, long-tail news documents with high ambiguity is detail, the participating systems are described, and additional analysis is presented to gain deeper insight into their performance.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: SemEval-2018 Task 5: Counting Events and Participants in the Long Tail

core.title: LSTM Networks Can Perform Dynamic Counting
core.venue: Proceedings of the Workshop on Deep Learning and Formal Languages: Building Bridges
core.summary: This work is the first study to introduce the shuffle languages to analyze the computational power of neural networks, and shows that a single-layer LSTM with only one hidden unit is practically sufficient for recognizing the Dyck-1 language.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: LSTM Networks Can Perform Dynamic Counting

core.title: Neural Databases
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: This paper describes NeuralDB, a database system with no pre-defined schema, in which updates and queries are given in natural language, and describes an algorithm that learns how to create the appropriate sets of facts to be fed into each of the Neural SPJ operators.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Neural Databases

core.title: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding
core.venue: BlackboxNLP@EMNLP
core.summary: A benchmark of nine diverse NLU tasks, an auxiliary dataset for probing models for understanding of specific linguistic phenomena, and an online platform for evaluating and comparing models, which favors models that can represent linguistic knowledge in a way that facilitates sample-efficient learning and effective knowledge-transfer across tasks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding

core.title: Know What You Don’t Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: SQuadRUn is a new dataset that combines the existing Stanford Question Answering Dataset (SQuAD) with over 50,000 unanswerable questions written adversarially by crowdworkers to look similar to answerable ones.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Know What You Don't Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD

core.title: Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: A stochastic variational inference and learning algorithm that scales to large datasets and, under some mild differentiability conditions, even works in the intractable case is introduced.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Auto-encoding variational bayes

core.title: Where’s My Head? Definition, Data Set, and Models for Numeric Fused-Head Identification and Resolution
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work explores the NFH phenomena in large corpora of English text and creates a data set and a highly accurate method for NFH identification; a 10k examples (1 M tokens) crowd-sourced data set of NFH resolution; and a neural baseline for theNFH resolution task.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Where's My Head? Definition, Data Set, and Models for Numeric Fused-Head Identification and Resolution

core.title: Japanese and Korean voice search
core.venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech, and Signal Processing
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Japanese and Korean voice search

core.title: Birds Have Four Legs?! NumerSense: Probing Numerical Commonsense Knowledge of Pre-trained Language Models
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: Investigating whether and to what extent one can induce numerical commonsense knowledge from PTLMs as well as the robustness of this process finds that this may not work for numerical Commonsense knowledge.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Birds have four legs?! NumerSense: Probing Numerical Commonsense Knowledge of Pre-Trained Language Models

core.title: Investigating the Limitations of Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks
core.summary: It is found that how a number is represented in its surface form has a strong influence on the model's accuracy, and this result bolsters evidence that subword tokenizers and positional encodings are components in current transformer designs that might need improvement.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Investigating the Limitations of the Transformers with Simple Arithmetic Tasks

core.title: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset
core.venue: NeurIPS Datasets and Benchmarks
core.summary: This work introduces MATH, a new dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems which can be used to teach models to generate answer derivations and explanations and shows that accuracy remains relatively low, even with enormous Transformer models.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset

core.title: Using the Output Embedding to Improve Language Models
core.venue: Conference of the European Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: The topmost weight matrix of neural network language models is studied and it is shown that this matrix constitutes a valid word embedding and a new method of regularizing the output embedding is offered.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Using the output embedding to improve language models

core.title: Are NLP Models really able to Solve Simple Math Word Problems?
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: It is shown that MWP solvers that do not have access to the question asked in the MWP can still solve a large fraction of MWPs, and models that treat MWPs as bag-of-words can also achieve surprisingly high accuracy.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Are NLP Models really able to Solve Simple Math Word Problems?

core.title: Knowledge Neurons in Pretrained Transformers
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This paper examines the fill-in-the-blank cloze task for BERT and proposes a knowledge attribution method to identify the neurons that express the fact, finding that the activation of such knowledge neurons is positively correlated to the expression of their corresponding facts.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Knowledge neurons in pretrained transformers

core.title: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work shows that feed-forward layers in transformer-based language models operate as key-value memories, where each key correlates with textual patterns in the training examples, and each value induces a distribution over the output vocabulary.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Transformer Feed-Forward Layers Are Key-Value Memories

core.title: On the number of k-skip-n-grams
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: The paper proves that the number of k-skip-n-grams for a corpus of size $L$ is$$\frac{Ln + n + k' - n^2 - nk'}{n} \cdot \binom{n-1+ k'}{ n-1}$$ where $k' = \min(L - n + 1, k)$.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: On the number of k-skip-n-grams

core.title: A Generalized Language Model as the Combination of Skipped n-grams and Modified Kneser Ney Smoothing
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A novel approach based on a systematic, recursive exploration of skip n-gram models which are interpolated using modified Kneser-Ney smoothing is introduced which generalizes language models as it contains the classical interpolation with lower order models as a special case.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: A Generalized Language Model as the Combination of Skipped n-grams and Modified Kneser Ney Smoothing

core.title: Hierarchical Phrase-Based Translation
core.venue: International Conference on Computational Logic
core.summary: A statistical machine translation model that uses hierarchical phrasesphrases that contain subphrasing that is formally a synchronous context-free grammar but is learned from a parallel text without any syntactic annotations is presented.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Hierarchical Phrase-Based Translation

core.title: Adaptor Grammars for Learning Non-Concatenative Morphology
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This paper contributes an approach for expressing non-concatenative morphological phenomena, such as stem derivation in Semitic languages, in terms of a mildly context-sensitive grammar formalism that offers a convenient level of modelling abstraction while remaining computationally tractable.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Adaptor Grammars for Learning Non-Concatenative Morphology

core.title: Learning to Generate Word- and Phrase-Embeddings for Efficient Phrase-Based Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This paper introduces a phrase-based NMT model built upon continuous-output NMT, in which the decoder generates embeddings of words or phrases, and shows that the model learns to translate phrases better, performing on par with state of the art phrase- based NMT.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Learning to Generate Word- and Phrase-Embeddings for Efficient Phrase-Based Neural Machine Translation

core.title: Phrase-Based & Neural Unsupervised Machine Translation
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work investigates how to learn to translate when having access to only large monolingual corpora in each language, and proposes two model variants, a neural and a phrase-based model, which are significantly better than methods from the literature, while being simpler and having fewer hyper-parameters.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Phrase-Based \& Neural Unsupervised Machine Translation

core.title: Translating Phrases in Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This work proposes a method to translate phrases in NMT by integrating a phrase memory storing target phrases from a phrase-based statistical machine translation (SMT) system into the encoder-decoder architecture of NMT.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Translating Phrases in Neural Machine Translation

core.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: SentencePiece, a language-independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer designed for Neural-based text processing, finds that it is possible to achieve comparable accuracy to direct subword training from raw sentences.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing

core.title: Finding the Optimal Vocabulary Size for Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Findings
core.summary: This work casts neural machine translation as a classification task in an autoregressive setting and analyzes the limitations of both classification and autoregression components, and reveals an explanation for why certain vocabulary sizes are better than others.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Finding the Optimal Vocabulary Size for Neural Machine Translation

core.title: The Google Similarity Distance
core.venue: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
core.summary: A new theory of similarity between words and phrases based on information distance and Kolmogorov complexity is presented, which is applied to construct a method to automatically extract similarity, the Google similarity distance, of Words and phrases from the WWW using Google page counts.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The Google Similarity Distance

core.title: Moses: Open Source Toolkit for Statistical Machine Translation
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: An open-source toolkit for statistical machine translation whose novel contributions are support for linguistically motivated factors, confusion network decoding, and efficient data formats for translation models and language models.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Moses: Open Source Toolkit for Statistical Machine Translation

core.title: The IIT Bombay English-Hindi Parallel Corpus
core.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
core.summary: The corpus has been pre-processed for machine translation, and baseline phrase-based SMT and NMT translation results on this corpus are reported, making it the largest publicly available English-Hindi parallel corpus.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The IIT Bombay English-Hindi Parallel Corpus

core.title: Findings of the 2019 Conference on Machine Translation (WMT19)
core.venue: Conference on Machine Translation
core.summary: This paper presents the results of the premier shared task organized alongside the Conference on Machine Translation (WMT) 2019, asked to build machine translation systems for any of 18 language pairs, to be evaluated on a test set of news stories.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Findings of the 2019 Conference on Machine Translation (WMT19)

core.title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
core.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A new approach based on the skipgram model, where each word is represented as a bag of character n-grams, with words being represented as the sum of these representations, which achieves state-of-the-art performance on word similarity and analogy tasks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Enriching word vectors with subword information

core.title: CodeBPE: Investigating Subtokenization Options for Large Language Model Pretraining on Source Code
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: This work proposes subtokenziation that reduces average length by 17% without downstream performance drop, and shows that a carefully chosen subtokenization may improve quality by 0.5-2%, possibly with some length increase.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: CodeBPE: Investigating Subtokenization Options for Large Language Model Pretraining on Source Code

core.title: Europarl: A Parallel Corpus for Statistical Machine Translation
core.venue: Machine Translation Summit
core.summary: A corpus of parallel text in 11 languages from the proceedings of the European Parliament is collected and its acquisition and application as training data for statistical machine translation (SMT) is focused on.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Europarl: A parallel corpus for statistical machine translation

core.title: Learn Your Tokens: Word-Pooled Tokenization for Language Modeling
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: This paper considers an alternative 'learn your tokens' scheme which utilizes the word boundary to pool bytes/characters into word representations, which are fed to the primary language model, before again decoding individual characters/bytes per word in parallel.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Learn Your Tokens: Word-Pooled Tokenization for Language Modeling

core.title: Making the Most of Text Semantics to Improve Biomedical Vision-Language Processing
core.venue: European Conference on Computer Vision
core.summary: It is shown that principled textual semantic modelling can substantially improve contrastive learning in self-supervised vision--language processing and is proposed as a self- supervised joint vision-- language approach with a focus on better text modelling.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Making the most of text semantics to improve biomedical vision--language processing

core.title: Scalable training of L1-regularized log-linear models
core.venue: International Conference on Machine Learning
core.summary: This work presents an algorithm Orthant-Wise Limited-memory Quasi-Newton (OWL-QN), based on L-BFGS, that can efficiently optimize the L1-regularized log-likelihood of log-linear models with millions of parameters.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Scalable training of L1-regularized log-linear models

core.title: Charformer: Fast Character Transformers via Gradient-based Subword Tokenization
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: A soft gradient-based subword tokenization module (GBST) that automatically learns latent subword representations from characters in a data-driven fashion is introduced that paves the way for highly performant token-free models that are trained completely end-to-end.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Charformer: Fast Character Transformers via Gradient-based Subword Tokenization

core.title: Learning Numeral Embedding
core.venue: Findings
core.summary: Two novel numeral embedding methods that can handle the out-of-vocabulary (OOV) problem for numerals are proposed and shown its effectiveness on four intrinsic and extrinsic tasks: word similarity, embedding numeracy, numeral prediction, and sequence labeling.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Learning Numeral Embeddings

core.title: The Biber Cognitive Estimation Test.
core.venue: Archives of Clinical Neuropsychology
core.summary: The Biber Cognitive Estimation Test (BCET), a 20-item test with five estimation questions in each of four categories: time/duration, quantity, weight, and distance, indicated that the BCET was able to distinguish between demented and intact elderly participants.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The Biber cognitive estimation test

core.title: Leap-Of-Thought: Teaching Pre-Trained Models to Systematically Reason Over Implicit Knowledge
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: This work provides a first demonstration that LMs can be trained to reliably perform systematic reasoning combining both implicit, pre-trained knowledge and explicit natural language statements, and demonstrates that models learn to effectively perform inference which involves implicit taxonomic and world knowledge, chaining and counting.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Leap-Of-Thought: Teaching Pre-Trained Models to Systematically Reason Over Implicit Knowledge

core.title: Children's understanding of counting.
core.venue: Cognition
core.summary: Children learn the meanings of smaller number words before larger ones within their counting range, up to the number three or four, indicating that children learn the cardinal word principle at roughly 3 1/2 years of age.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Children's understanding of counting

core.title: Automating Potato Leaf Disease Detection with Lightning-Fast CNNs: Precision using PyTorch Lightning
core.venue: 2024 5th International Conference on Smart Electronics and Communication (ICOSEC)
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: PyTorch Lightning

core.title: A Framework for Learning Predictive Structures from Multiple Tasks and Unlabeled Data
core.venue: Journal of machine learning research
core.summary: This paper presents a general framework in which the structural learning problem can be formulated and analyzed theoretically, and relate it to learning with unlabeled data, and algorithms for structural learning will be proposed, and computational issues will be investigated.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: A Framework for Learning Predictive Structures from Multiple Tasks and Unlabeled Data

core.title: On the Usability of Transformers-based Models for a French Question-Answering Task
core.venue: Recent Advances in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: A state-of-the-art of the efforts dedicated to the usability of Transformer-based models are established and improvements on the question-answering performances of French language which have few resources are proposed.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: On the Usability of Transformers-based models for a French Question-Answering task

core.title: A Vocabulary-Free Multilingual Neural Tokenizer for End-to-End Task Learning
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: A Vocabulary-Free Multilingual Neural Tokenizer for End-to-End Task Learning

core.title: What do tokens know about their characters and how do they know it?
core.venue: Proceedings of the 2022 Conference of the North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: What do tokens know about their characters and how do they know it?

core.title: arabic-digital-humanities/root-extraction-validation-data: 0.1.0
core.venue: Figshare
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: arabic-digital-humanities/root-extraction- validation-data: 0.1.0

core.title: What is the best recipe for character-level encoder-only modelling?
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: What is the best recipe for character-level encoder-only modelling?

core.title: Tokenization with Factorized Subword Encoding
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Tokenization with Factorized Subword Encoding

core.title: How Much Coffee Was Consumed During EMNLP 2019? Fermi Problems: A New\n Reasoning Challenge for AI
core.venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: How much coffee was consumed during EMNLP 2019? fermi problems: A new reasoning challenge for AI

core.title: ByT5: Towards a token-free future with pre-trained byte-to-byte models
core.venue: arXiv (Cornell University)
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: ByT5: Towards a token-free future with pre-trained byte-to-byte models

core.title: How much coffee was consumed during EMNLP 2019? Fermi Problems: A New Reasoning Challenge for AI
core.venue: Proceedings of the 2021 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: How much coffee was consumed during EMNLP 2019? Fermi Problems: A New Reasoning Challenge for AI

core.title: Paying Attention to Multi-Word Expressions in Neural Machine Translation
core.venue: Machine Translation Summit
core.summary: Results of experiments on investigating NMT attention allocation to the MWEs and improving automated translation of sentences that contain MWES in English->Latvian and English->Czech NMT systems are presented.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Paying Attention to Multi-Word Expressions in Neural Machine Translation

core.title: Injecting Numerical Reasoning Skills into Language Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work shows that numerical reasoning is amenable to automatic data generation, and thus one can inject this skill into pre-trained LMs, by generating large amounts of data, and training in a multi-task setup.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Injecting Numerical Reasoning Skills into Language Models

core.title: Probing for Multilingual Numerical Understanding in Transformer-Based Language Models
core.venue: BlackboxNLP Workshop on Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
core.summary: Novel multilingual probing tasks tested on DistilBERT, XLM, and BERT find evidence that the information encoded in these pretrained models’ embeddings is sufficient for grammaticality judgments but generally not for value comparisons.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Probing for Multilingual Numerical Understanding in Transformer-Based Language Models

core.title: Analysing Mathematical Reasoning Abilities of Neural Models
core.venue: International Conference on Learning Representations
core.summary: This paper conducts a comprehensive analysis of models from two broad classes of the most powerful sequence-to-sequence architectures and finds notable differences in their ability to resolve mathematical problems and generalize their knowledge.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Analysing Mathematical Reasoning Abilities of Neural Models

core.title: On the Computational Power of Transformers and Its Implications in Sequence Modeling
core.venue: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
core.summary: This paper provides an alternate and simpler proof to show that vanilla Transformers are Turing-complete and proves that Transformers with only positional masking and without any positional encoding are also Turing- complete.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: On the Computational Power of Transformers and Its Implications in Sequence Modeling

core.title: HuggingFace's Transformers: State-of-the-art Natural Language Processing
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: The \textit{Transformers} library is an open-source library that consists of carefully engineered state-of-the art Transformer architectures under a unified API and a curated collection of pretrained models made by and available for the community.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Transformers: State-of-the-Art Natural Language Processing

core.title: Can Chatgpt Improve Investment Decision? From a Portfolio Management Perspective
core.venue: Social Science Research Network
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Can Chatgpt Improve Investment Decision? From a Portfolio Management Perspective

core.title: Attention is All you Need
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: A new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely is proposed, which generalizes well to other tasks by applying it successfully to English constituency parsing both with large and limited training data.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Attention is all you need

core.title: NASA publications manual 1974
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Publications Manual

core.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
core.summary: The general task-agnostic model outperforms discriminatively trained models that use architectures speciﬁcally crafted for each task, improving upon the state of the art in 9 out of the 12 tasks studied.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Improving language understanding by generative pre-training

core.title: The Society of Mind
core.venue: Personalist Forum
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Society of mind

core.title: The Bitter Lesson Learned from 2,000+ Multilingual Benchmarks
core.venue: arXiv.org
core.summary: Examining over 2,000 multilingual (non-English) benchmarks from 148 countries, published between 2021 and 2024, reveals that, despite significant investments amounting to tens of millions of dollars, English remains significantly overrepresented in these benchmarks.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The bitter lesson

core.title: The Number Sense: How the Mind Creates Mathematics.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: The number sense: How the mind creates mathematics

core.title: A Fact-aligned Corpus of Numerical Expressions
core.venue: International Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation
core.summary: A corpus of numerical expressions developed as part of the NUMGEN project is described, showing that when a fact is mentioned more than once in a text, there is a clear tendency for precision to increase from first to subsequent mentions, and for mathematical level either to remain constant or to increase.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: A Fact-aligned Corpus of Numerical Expressions

core.title: Numeral Understanding in Financial Tweets for Fine-Grained Crowd-Based Forecasting
core.venue: International Conference on Wirtschaftsinformatik
core.summary: This work is the first attempt to understand numerals in financial social media data, and it provides the first comparison of fine-grained opinion of individual investors and analysts based on their forecast price.

core.title: QuaRel: A Dataset and Models for Answering Questions about Qualitative Relationships
core.venue: AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
core.summary: This work makes inroads into answering complex, qualitative questions that require reasoning, and scaling to new relationships at low cost, with two novel models for this task built as extensions of type-constrained semantic parsing.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Quarel: A dataset and models for answering questions about qualitative relationships

core.title: SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems

core.title: Clustering of Self-Organizing Map

core.title: Neural Arithmetic Logic Units
core.venue: Neural Information Processing Systems
core.summary: Experiments show that NALU-enhanced neural networks can learn to track time, perform arithmetic over images of numbers, translate numerical language into real-valued scalars, execute computer code, and count objects in images.
core.source: avi-thesis.bib: Neural arithmetic logic units

core.title: Language Combinatorics: A Sentence Pattern Extraction Architecture Based on Combinatorial Explosion
core.summary: A language independent architecture for extracting from sentences more sophisticated patterns than n-grams is presented, in which a “sentence pattern” is considered as n-element ordered combination of sentence elements.

core.title: News from OPUS — A collection of multilingual parallel corpora with tools and interfaces

core.title: Risk Factors That Matter: Textual Analysis of Risk Disclosures for the Cross-Section of Returns

core.title: Visual sense of number vs. sense of magnitude in humans and machines
